DILG BAGONG PIL'PINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. S. 2024 FEB 2 6 2025 MR. LAWRENCE VERGARA vergaralawrence@qmail.com Hermosa, Bataan Dear Mr. Vergara: This has reference to the electronic mail dated 8 January 2025 requesting the Departments opinion relative to the regulatory power of the Municipal Mayor of Hermosa, Bataan. You maintain that the mayor has not issued a Business Permit to the businesses located along the Roman Super Hi-way of Hermosa, Bataan. The Office of the Mayor or the Municipality Engineering Office requested business or landowners to provide an 8-meter parking space from its private property line. Contrary to last yeads instruction from the Municipal Administrator of a 5-meter parking space setback which is in accordance with the National Building Code. Further, no notice of hearing has been conducted to inform small business owners regarding the matter. Hence, this point of clarification. We discuss. At the outset, a mayor's or business permit is issued primarily to regulate the conduct of business within a locality with the end view that all businesses operating therein are in accordance with law or ordinancel. One of the general requirements for a mayor's permit is the submission of a building permit. In processing an application for a building permit, the Building Official sees to it that the applicant satisfies and conforms with approved standard requirements on zoning and land use, lines and grades, structural design, sanitary and sewerage, environmental health, electrical and mechanical safety as well as with other rules and regulations promulgated in accordance with the provisions of the Code2. The National Building Code and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) specify minimum setback requirements. As an initial finding, the general setback requirement for commercial establishments ranges from 5.0 meters to 8.0 meters depending on the Road Right-of-Way width.3 Given the limited information provided, we are unable to determine whether the required 8-meter parking space is in accordance with the National Building Code. Moreover, we also recognize the power and function of the Sangguniang Bayan, consistent with 1 DILG LO No. 51 s. 2012. 2 Sec. 303, PD 1096, National Building Code of the Philippines. 3 Table VIII.2, Implementing Rules and Regulations of the National Building Code "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

the Local Govemment Code, to prescribe reasonable limits and restraints on the use of property within the jurisdiction of the municipality4 Anent the representation that due process was not observed, not all ordinances require the conduct of public hearing. Prior public hearings are required where (1) local government site, offices and facilities are to be transferred; (2) reclassification of agricultural lands; (3) contribution of funds, real estate, equipment and other kinds of property and appointment or assignment of personnel in support of undertakings commonly beneficial to local govemment units which have grouped themselves, consolidated or coordinated their efforts, services and resources; (4) levy of taxes, fees or charges on any base or subject not otherwise specially enumerated in the Local Govemment Code as taxed under the NIRC, as amended, or other applicable laws; and (5) enactment of local tax ordinances and revenue measures5. To our understanding, the point of contention here does not fall under any of the categories mentioned above. Moreover, the fact that no notice of hearing was conducted does not affect the validity of the subject ordinance. Lastly, we advise you to coordinate with your LGU and seek clarification as to the basis of the 8- meter parking requirement. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the—etary: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs 4 sec. 447. RA 7160, Local Government Code of 1991.
